title: The Priest the Thief and the Ghost

keywords: the brahmin the thief and the ghost
full_text:
In a secluded forest hermitage lived an impoverished, austere Priest named Drona, who had renounced all worldly luxury. An admirer had presented him with two young calves, which the holy man nourished with wild grass and clean spring water until they grew into two magnificent, sleek, muscular white bullocks.

A professional highway thief observed the fat animals and resolved: 'Tonight I will steal those two fine bullocks and sell them in the royal bazaar.'

As the thief was walking down the dark, wooded trail toward the hermitage, he encountered an awful specter: a terrifying ghost, or the ancient elder-Rakshasa, with hollow sunken eyes, fangs like sharp chisels, skin the color of dry smoke, and protruding ribs.

Though his hair stood on end, the thief asked: 'Who are you, terrifying apparition?'

The ghost replied: 'I am a hungry ghost who eats once every six nights. Tonight is my sixth night, and I am walking to the hermitage to devour the pious Priest Drona. Who are you?'

The thief felt his courage return: 'I am a thief! I am going to the same cottage to steal his two fat bullocks! Let us walk together.'

Arriving at the hermitage, they slipped through the bamboo wattle. The two fat bullocks were tethered peacefully under the thatched shed, while the pious Priest slept deeply on his grass mat on the veranda, exhausted from his day of chanting sacred texts.

The ghost stepped forward, extending his bony claws: 'Stand aside, thief! I will devour the Priest first while he is asleep!'

The thief seized the ghost's arm: 'No! If you attempt to seize him, he may utter a cry and wake the villagers! If the peasants rush in with clubs, I will not be able to drive off the cattle! Let me untie the bullocks and lead them into the road first, and then you may devour the Priest at your leisure!'

The ghost snarled: 'If you untie the cattle first, their clattering hooves will awaken the Priest! If he wakes, he will recite sacred mantras, and I will be burned to ashes! I will eat him now!'

'No, the cattle come first!' hissed the thief.

Their stubborn argument grew so loud and furious that the sleeping Priest sat up on his mat.

Seeing the holy man awake, the thief immediately shouted: 'Priest, beware! This hungry ghost has come to devour you!'

The ghost shrieked: 'Priest, beware! This thief has come to steal your two fat bullocks!'

Rising calmly from his mat, the Priest recited the powerful Gayatri and protective Vedic mantras. Hearing the sacred syllables, the ghost shrieked in agony and dissolved into the mist; while the Priest seized his heavy staff and drove the terrified thief out of the garden.

Thus Vishnu Sharma taught:
"When wicked thieves and hungry ghosts in mutual hatred clash,
Their secret enterprise dissolves like embers into ash;
The righteous man who keeps his faith and speaks the sacred word,
Finds safety from the quarreling foe before his voice is heard."
moral: When evil forces conspire against the virtuous, their own mutual jealousy frustrates their wicked intent.
